cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has been bringing God's message to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Now the LORD tells Moses to get up early in the morning. No snooze button, friend, NONE.

cards.question: Where does the LORD tell Moses to go stand before Pharaoh that morning?

answers.text: Where Pharaoh goes out to the water
Where Pharaoh sits on his throne
Where Pharaoh rides out in his chariot

cards.text: The LORD's message is that line again: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." And if Pharaoh still won't, something is headed his way.

cards.question: If Pharaoh won't let the people go, what does the LORD say He'll send?
The LORD says the flies will stay out in the fields, away from the houses.

cards.text: Then the LORD says something new: on that day, one place gets special treatment. The VIP section, friend!

cards.question: Which land does the LORD say will have no swarms of flies?
Why does the LORD say He'll keep the flies out of the place where His people live?

answers.text: So Pharaoh will know the LORD is in the land
So the Israelites can hide there from Pharaoh
So Moses will have a safe place to pray

cards.question: Flies everywhere except where God's people live. The LORD tells Pharaoh He will make a ___ between His people and Pharaoh's people.

cards.text: And the LORD did so: thick swarms of flies pour into Pharaoh's palace and his officials' houses, and all through Egypt the land is ruined. I once spent an HOUR swinging my mustache at ONE fly in my bakery, so I can't even imagine.
Pharaoh calls in Moses and Aaron, Moses' brother. And with flies buzzing in his ears, Pharaoh is suddenly ready to talk.

cards.question: What does Pharaoh offer Moses and Aaron?

answers.text: Go sacrifice to your God within this land
Go sacrifice and never come back here
Send only your elders to go sacrifice

cards.question: Moses says no to sacrificing inside Egypt. What reason does he give Pharaoh?

answers.text: Their sacrifices would be detestable to the Egyptians
The LORD only accepts their sacrifices in Goshen
Egypt has no altar built for the LORD their God

cards.question: Moses tells Pharaoh they must make a ___-day journey into the ___ to sacrifice to the LORD their God.

cards.text: Pharaoh says they can go sacrifice in the wilderness, but they must not go very far. Then in the SAME breath, bargaining AND asking a favor: "Now pray for me."

cards.question: Moses agrees to pray for Pharaoh, but he warns Pharaoh not to act deceitfully again.
Moses prays, and the LORD does as Moses asked. How many flies are left on Pharaoh and his people?

answers.text: Only the ones in the palace

cards.question: Once the flies are gone, Pharaoh keeps his word and lets the people go.

cards.text: Then the LORD sends Moses back to Pharaoh with a message from "the LORD, the God of the Hebrews": "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me." If Pharaoh keeps refusing, the hand of the LORD is coming. Moses has walked this road so many times, friend, he could do it with his eyes closed.

cards.question: The hand of the LORD will bring a severe plague on Egypt's ___ in the field.

cards.text: Horses, donkeys, camels, herds and flocks. And remember that line God drew with the flies? He draws it again, this time between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt.

cards.question: The LORD says a few of Israel's animals will still die, just fewer than Egypt's.
The LORD even sets a time for the plague on the livestock. When does He say it will happen?

cards.text: The next day, the LORD does just that: all the livestock of the Egyptians die, but not one animal belonging to the Israelites dies. The LORD said tomorrow, friend, and the LORD MEANT tomorrow.

cards.question: Pharaoh wants to know about Israel's animals. How does he find out none of them died?

answers.text: He asks his magicians to look

cards.question: None of Israel's livestock died. But Pharaoh's heart was ___, and he would not let the people go.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses and Aaron to grab handfuls of soot from the furnace. Friend, I KNOW soot, because I've left a batch in the oven too long more times than I can count.

cards.question: What is Moses supposed to do with the soot, right in Pharaoh's sight?
The soot will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt. What will that dust cause?

answers.text: Festering boils on man and beast
Hail on every field in Egypt

cards.text: So they take the soot and stand before Pharaoh, and Moses tosses it into the air. Festering boils break out on man and beast, all from ONE toss, friend.

cards.question: Pharaoh's magicians copy the boils with their magic arts.
Pharaoh's magicians can't even stand before Moses. Why not?

answers.text: Boils had broken out on them too
Pharaoh had sent them all away
They had run off to Goshen

cards.question: This time, the ___ hardens Pharaoh's heart, and Pharaoh won't listen to Moses and Aaron.

cards.text: Just as the LORD had said to Moses. Flies, livestock, boils, and Pharaoh still won't listen, so trust me, friend, this story is far from over.

findings.problem: "And with flies buzzing in his ears, Pharaoh is suddenly ready to talk" gives a reason for Pharaoh summoning Moses and Aaron. Exodus 8:25 only says Pharaoh summoned them and made an offer. It never says the flies are why.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Exodus 8:32 says Pharaoh "hardened his heart this time as well." No card tells the baker this. The card only asks whether he lets the people go. The passage moves from Pharaoh hardening his own heart (8:32), to his heart being hardened (9:7), to the LORD hardening it (9:12). Stop 2 card 15 then says "This time, the ___ hardens Pharaoh's heart," which sets up a contrast the baker was never given.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This is not the passage's opening card, and it has three sentences: the message, the warning, and the joke about Moses walking the road with his eyes closed. It needs to be cut to two, or split into two cards.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "all from ONE toss" is stated as fact and adds a count the text doesn't give. Exodus 9:8 says to take "handfuls" of soot, and 9:10 says Moses "tossed it into the air." Neither verse says how many tosses.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Most of stop 2's choice cards can only be answered by luck. Cards 2 (livestock), 5 (tomorrow), 7 (sends officials), 10 (toss it into the air), 11 (boils) and 13 (magicians copy the boils) all have no setup the baker could reason from. That is 6 of 10. Card 13 brings in the magicians with no setup at all. Card 5 could become an informed guess if stop 1 told the baker that the flies sign was set for "tomorrow" (Exodus 8:23), which is currently left out.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
